column1: # Atlas search: what people type, and what it must mean. One query per line.
# Columns, tab-separated: lang, query, expect, freq, note. expect lists the facts the parse must have, joined by " ; ".
# expect holds only what the query says; what the app should infer or do is in note.
# - "near me", "nearby", "around here", "in de buurt", "in der Nähe", "près d'ici" are the default area and add no fact.
# - A superlative is a sort; limit= only when the query says a number ("3 closest").
# - A named place after near, next to, by, bij, bei, près de is near=name=X; after in, on, at, op, im, à it is area=X (town, district, park, street, station, postcode).

# - want= when an often unmapped property qualifies a kind (toilets, internet_access, power_supply, changing_table, highchair, kids_area, dog and wheelchair at venues, shade, air_conditioning, breakfast, real_fire, payment:*): places that say nothing stay, as unsure. tag= is a firm condition, and so is a property searched on its own.
# - Vague wishes are prefer=: kid friendly is highchair and kids_area; quiet is no live music, away from bars and busy roads.
# - tag=brand!=* means no brand tag (not a chain); tag=key!=value also passes places without the key; a bare tag=key means the key is set.
# - Reference clock: Tuesday 2026-11-03 14:00 Europe/Amsterdam. today = Tu, tomorrow = We, early = 07:00, morning = 09:00, lunch = 12:00, tonight = 20:30, late and at night = 23:00 (open=late).
# - "Open until T", "open after T", "past T" and "opens before T" are open=T (closing at T counts); "closes before T" and "opens after T" are closes=T and opens=T, one-sided.
# - Years: the 17th century is start_date>=1600 and <1700; older than 300 years is start_date<1726; newly built is >=2021; the last 10 years is >=2016.
# - Speeds: walking 80 m/min, cycling 250 m/min, driving 600 m/min; walking distance is within=1200; a 5-minute walk is within=400.
# - Cheap is sort=CHEAPEST: prices are seldom mapped, so the note says what to rank on. Dates and public holidays add only the kind; the note names the PH rule.
# - route=A->B for directions and for "on the way to"; an end is here, home, work, a name, or a kind (the nearest one). The travel mode is in the note.
# - intent= names an activity; the note lists what it expands to and when it depends on weather or season.
# - What the model cannot express yet is written as it should be (area=@neighbourhood) or as unsupported=WHY.

# - notarea=X is an area kept out of; closed=Mo closed all that day by the hours; than=height>Name compares with another place; per= tells a count by place; via=A|B are a way's stops in order; near=k=v+k2=v2 is one place with both tags.
